original_value: In recent years, wireless sensor networks (WSNs) have become an active area of research for monitoring physical and environmental conditions. Due to the interdependence of sensors, a functional anomaly in one sensor can cause a functional anomaly in another sensor, which can further lead to the malfunctioning of the entire sensor network. Existing research work has analysed faulty sensor anomalies but fails to show the effectiveness throughout the entire interdependent network system. In this article, a dictionary learning algorithm based on a non-negative constraint is developed, and a sparse representation anomaly node detection method for sensor networks is proposed based on the dictionary learning. Through experiment on a specific thermal power plant in China, we verify the robustness of our proposed method in detecting abnormal nodes against four state of the art approaches and proved our method is more robust. Furthermore, the experiments are conducted on the obtained abnormal nodes to prove the interdependence of multi-layer sensor networks and reveal the conditions and causes of a system crash.

result.paraphrase: Wireless sensor networks (WSNs) have recently become a major research focus for monitoring physical and environmental conditions. Because sensors depend on one another, a fault in one sensor may trigger faults in others and eventually lead to failure of the whole network. Prior studies have examined faulty sensor anomalies, but they do not demonstrate effectiveness across the full interdependent network system. In this article, we develop a dictionary learning algorithm with a non-negative constraint and, based on it, propose a sparse-representation anomaly node detection method for sensor networks. Experiments on a specific thermal power plant in China show that our method is more robust than four state-of-the-art approaches in detecting abnormal nodes. In addition, experiments on the detected abnormal nodes confirm the interdependence of multi-layer sensor networks and reveal the conditions and causes of a system crash.
